A.explanation: Amplitude is the full maximum displacement from equilibrium, so halving it would give only half the amplitude.

B.explanation: Distance apart of neighbouring bars depends on the displacements of two different particles, not the displacement of one particle from rest.

C.explanation: Amplitude is defined as the maximum displacement of a vibrating particle from its equilibrium position at rest.

D.explanation: Maximum distance apart measures separation between two bars in a rarefaction, not displacement of one bar from its top-row position.

walkthrough: The top row shows the equilibrium positions with evenly spaced bars at rest, and the lower row shows the same bars displaced left and right by the longitudinal wave.
For a progressive wave, amplitude is defined as the maximum displacement $x_{max}$ of a single oscillating particle from its equilibrium position.
Because the wave is longitudinal and travels left to right, each particle oscillates left and right, so its displacement is the horizontal shift from its top-row position.
To find it, align each lower bar with its original upper bar and measure the horizontal shift, then take the largest shift seen in compressions and rarefactions.
That largest shift from rest is the amplitude. This is option C.
